relevance_note: Two siblings and their mother carry a PSTPIP1 variant with individual-level detail: "a heterozygous rare missense mutation of unknown significance in the two patients and in the mother, the p.(Val408Ile) in the exon 15 of the PSTPIP1 gene".
method_note: Read the whole case report by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. In-scope people: Patient 1 and Patient 2 (PSTPIP1 p.(Val408Ile) heterozygous), their mother (carries the same PSTPIP1 variant, symptomatic), their father (tested negative for PSTPIP1) and their 18-year-old sister (tested only for MEFV as reported; her PSTPIP1 status is not reported). Relatives are labelled relative to Patient 1 although they are equally relatives of Patient 2. MEFV p.M680I rows are recorded as variants in another gene attributed unambiguously to each person (homozygous in both patients; heterozygous in both parents and the sister). MEFV inheritance in the patients is left 'not reported' because both parents carry it and the enum has no biallelic option; the parental statement is quoted. The PSTPIP1 variant in the patients is recorded as 'inherited maternal' because the mother carries the same variant and the father was negative. The 'in-silico prediction to be damaging' is not a functional assay and was not recorded as functional evidence. Laboratory abnormalities (AST, ALT, CRP, ESR, leucocytosis with neutrophilia, SAA) and the 'retrosternal and thoracic pain' and 'undefined dermatitis at the hands' come from statements naming both patients ('both patients', 'The two patients', 'two siblings') and were recorded for each as stated. Negative serologies for EBV, Parvovirus, HHV6, Mycoplasma and Streptococcus were an infection work-up, not recorded as phenotypic features. The authors say the skin lesions 'were not typical of PAPA Syndrome' and treat the PSTPIP1 variant as a possible modifier allele; disease label 'PAPA and FMF' is taken from the title. n_patients_reported = 3 counts the two patients and the mother named as PSTPIP1 carriers; the authors give no single number. Neutrophilia was not used to exclude neutropenia. No contradictions found.
